artists.biography: Charles Bradley (born 1948, Gainesville, Florida), commonly referred to as "The Screaming Eagle of Soul," is a funk/soul/R&B singer signed to the Daptone Records label under the Dunham Records division. His performances and recording style are consistent with Daptone's revivalist approach, celebrating the feel of funk and soul music from the 1960s and 1970s. One review stated that Bradley "echoes the evocative delivery of Otis Redding". He is the subject of a documentary, Soul of America, that premiered at SXSW in 2012.
artists.name: Charles Bradley

artists.biography:
The Menahan Street Band is a Brooklyn, New York-based instrumental band formed in 2007, that plays funk and soul music. The band features musicians from Antibalas, El Michels Affair, Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings and the Budos Band. The group was founded by Thomas Brenneck while living in an apartment on Menahan St. in the Brooklyn neighborhood of Bushwick. Their debut album, Make the Road by Walking, was released in 2008 on Dunham, a sublabel of Daptone Records.

After Jay Z sampled the album's title track for his hit single "Roc Boys (And the Winner Is…)", the band invested their royalty money from the song in building a studio. Brenneck launched the all-analog Dunham Sound Studios, and the band worked there for many months on the completion of their 2012 sophomore album The Crossing.

perplexity.description:
No Time for Dreaming, released in 2011 on Dunham and Daptone Records, is the debut studio album by American soul and funk singer Charles Bradley. The album is a powerful example of retro soul, drawing heavily on the sounds of 1960s and 1970s funk and soul, with lush arrangements by The Menahan Street Band and production that emphasizes vintage warmth and authenticity. Bradley’s impassioned, raw vocals echo the emotive delivery of legends like Otis Redding, earning him the nickname "The Screaming Eagle of Soul." The album’s themes center on love, hardship, and resilience, with standout tracks such as "The World (Is Going Up In Flames)," "Why Is It So Hard?," and "Heartaches and Pain" showcasing both his vocal prowess and the band’s tight, evocative instrumentation.

As Bradley’s first full-length release at the age of 62, No Time for Dreaming marked a late but significant breakthrough in his career, establishing him as a leading figure in the soul revival movement. The album was widely praised for its emotional depth and stylistic fidelity to classic soul, with critics highlighting its heartfelt performances and timeless sound. Though it did not achieve mainstream commercial success, it garnered strong critical acclaim and a devoted following, setting the stage for Bradley’s subsequent albums and cementing his legacy as a genuine voice in contemporary soul music.
